what_matters.head: Chip stocks fell hard on Thursday: the chip fund lost 6.8%, 2.7× its usual day, and the Nasdaq 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June.
what_matters.detail: Reuters tied the sell-off to Meta's results, which revived worry about the cost of the AI build-out. With its results on Wednesday, Meta announced a new class of listed shares without votes, to be handed to shareholders one for each share they hold; the charter change takes effect on 19 Jan 2027, with the payout date still to be set, and Meta says it may use the new shares to raise money, pay staff and buy companies. Reuters said the plan revived concern over Meta's growing spending commitments. The Motley Fool also pointed to higher oil, which feeds inflation and keeps borrowing costs high for companies spending heavily on AI. Nine names fell 2× their usual day or more (movers below).

what_matters.tag_note: Nokia · first US session after its results
what_matters.head: Nokia fell 14.8% in New York, 4.0× its usual day, after it cut its forecast for how much of its profit turns into cash this year.
what_matters.detail: It now expects 2026 free cash flow of 35–55% of its comparable operating profit, down from 55–75%. Free cash flow was about −€99M in the quarter, and it raised its 2026 restructuring charges to €1.1B (Investing.com). It kept its 2026 operating profit forecast unchanged, not raised; The Motley Fool also pointed to the shares' high valuation going in and the day's AI sell-off.

what_matters.tag_note: Bloom Energy · results after Thursday's US close
what_matters.head: Bloom Energy raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $4.4–4.6B, from $3.9–4.2B, after third-quarter revenue of $1.24B, up 138% from a year earlier.
what_matters.detail: Analysts expected revenue of about $1.1B. Earnings per share were $0.94 against the $0.67 analysts expected. It also forecast 2026 earnings per share of $3.10–3.40 and a 34% gross margin. The shares had already fallen 8.7% in Thursday's sell-off before the results, and the run's after-hours quote was 6.9% lower again. Stocktwits pointed to cash flow: record capital spending of $231M so far this year, and net cash flow of about −$180M. No backlog figure was given; the chief executive said the backlog is growing faster than revenue.

after_data.text: Western Digital, not held, reported after Thursday's close: revenue rose 55% to $4.38B, above the $4.14B analysts expected, and it forecast $5.0–5.2B for this quarter. Its shares rose about 4% at first, then fell about 8% after hours once the call flagged rising input costs and capital spending set somewhat higher as a share of revenue over the next two years (Investing.com). Not in Thursday's US prices for Sandisk or Micron.

Brent reached $114, a five-month high, in Asian trade on Friday, and Taiwan's market was closed for a typhoon (Reuters). Micron's Taoyuan union had its second round of talks set for Friday, or Tuesday 27 Oct if a typhoon cancelled them (United Daily News, 22 Oct); no report on whether they went ahead was found.

latest.tape_note: US stocks fell on Thursday: the S&P 500 lost 1.2%, while the Dow ended 12 points higher (Reuters). Investors bought Treasuries as stocks fell: the 10-year yield dropped 19 basis points to 4.95%, its biggest one-day fall since March 2023. By Friday, traders' odds of a Fed rate rise in December had fallen to 85%, from fully priced, and they had taken out nearly all of the rise they expected next year (Reuters). Brent settled 4% higher at $113.17 after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia (Reuters). Gold fell 2.2% and VIX rose to 19.
latest.tonight: No major US economic release and no watchlist results tonight. Next week: SK Hynix, Alphabet and Microsoft report on 28 Oct, the Fed decides early on Thursday 29 Oct SGT, and Samsung, Amazon, Intel, Sandisk, AXT and Aixtron report on 29 Oct.

recent.headline: Chip stocks fell hard on Thursday: the chip fund lost 6.8%, 2.7× its usual day, and the Nasdaq 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June.
Meta's revenue beat its own forecast, but a $9.9B legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83, against the $5.46 analysts expected. The shares rose 2.1% after hours.
After Tuesday's US close, Super Micro raised its estimate of last quarter's revenue to $18.5–19.5B, from its forecast of $14.5–15.5B, citing demand for AI platforms.
Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.
